marta.desiderio: That Gino doesn't leave the way Ernesto did.

piero.desiderio: To give back what I keep.

gino.desiderio: To see the lighthouse lantern lit from inside.

bepi.desiderio: To say goodbye to Nina properly.

nina.desiderio: To study in Venice and become a teacher.

lunardi.desiderio: That the island calls me by my name.

livia.ruolo: the woman in the black shawl, 38

clotilde.ruolo: the grandmother, lacemaker for sixty years

molo.descrizione: Mooring posts, boats, the morning and evening ferry.

forno.descrizione: The mouth of Marta's oven. Bread at six.

piazza.descrizione: The wellhead, the benches, the market from nine to eleven.

chiesa.descrizione: The churchyard and the bell tower, whose clock strikes out of tune.

farmacia.descrizione: The counter and the jars. Closed, until someone comes.

faro.descrizione: White and red on the rocks. The light from six in the evening.

stanza.descrizione: The lace pillow on its stand, the empty chair, the chest.

incrocio.testo: Two threads that meet swap places. Each thread crosses at most once an hour, and only its neighbour.
incrocio.margine: The Fondamenta is narrow: to get by, you have to talk.

spillo.testo: A brass pin is an appointment: it does not move. The hour cannot be set until it is kept.
spillo.margine: Bread at six, mass at eleven. Everything else can change.

sopraDa.testo: A letter passes from the thread on top to the one below. Once it reaches its addressee, it stays. Tap a crossing to flip it.
sopraDa.margine: Who is on top, gives. Who is below, receives. It is not a matter of honour.

voce.testo: A rumour copies both ways: after the crossing both of them know it, and nobody unlearns it.

matassa.testo: A night's thread is counted. Each crossing costs one arm's length of skein; flipping it costs nothing.

molo.testo: At boat time whoever is in the edge column leaves the lace, and whoever arrives takes their place.
molo.margine: At boat time, whoever is at the Pier goes away.

segreto.testo: A secret passes only from the thread on top to the one below. Whoever confides it, keeps it.

pozzo.testo: Don Piero takes everything and gives nothing: letters, rumours, secrets. Letters not meant for him stay with him.
pozzo.margine: Don Piero is a well. But even wells fill up.

febbre.testo: If one of the two is ill, after the crossing both are. The pharmacist, when he is on top, heals.

nodo.testo: Two threads holding a grudge give each other nothing when they cross: they knot, and stay still the next hour.
nodo.margine: Two who hate each other, if they meet, stand still.

nome.testo: Every night I pin my name on one thread, and it spreads like a rumour. Whoever doesn't get it forgets me a little.

nero.testo: It moves by itself, one step an hour, towards whoever it seeks. It is always on top, and I see it coming an hour early.

marea.testo: During high water the threads in flooded columns stay still: nobody gets in, nobody gets out.
marea.margine: High water makes the island smaller.

puntoAperto.testo: Nobody is crossed. You plant occasions, and the threads meet by themselves, following what they want.
puntoAperto.margine: I did not have the courage.

martaTeresa.titolo: Why don't Marta and Teresa speak to each other?

merletto_avorio.descrizione: An ivory thread that belongs to nobody breaks off at three, cut clean.

libro_punti.descrizione: Worn leather, handwritten pages. In the margins, grandmother's sepia hand.

bottiglia.descrizione: The lagoon brought it to the door. Inside, a rolled sheet signed "L.".

fuso_faro.nome: A bobbin carved like a lighthouse
fuso_faro.descrizione: Zeno lost it. Inside, carved small, there is an initial: "L.".

pagina_strappata.descrizione: It comes from the Book of Stitches. It shows a stitch I don't know, and no explanation.

bottiglia_nodo_nero.descrizione: No letter. Inside, a knot of black thread.

fascio_lettere.descrizione: Three readable letters, and a hundred and sixty-five more. One a month, for fourteen years.

nastro_nonna.descrizione: The leftover ivory thread, carefully wound.

incontro.1: Oh, dear, what a day! I saw everyone, and everyone saw me.
incontro.2: A chat on the Fondamenta is worth more than a letter, dear.

consegna.1: Delivered by hand, dear. Thirty years of post and never a lost envelope.
consegna.2: The post always arrives. Sometimes late, but it arrives.

copia.1: I never tell anyone, dear. Only those who ask.
copia.2: A rumour, dear, is like bread: if you don't pass it on, it goes stale.

legge.1: I didn't read it, dear. I just… held it up to the light.
legge.2: An open envelope is an envelope that wants to talk.

stranezza.1: Marta always goes over me. Always. For thirty years.
stranezza.2: Look how she avoids me, dear. As if I had the plague.

nodo.1: Marta, look at me. No? Fine. That's fine.
nodo.2: We stood in the middle of the Fondamenta like two mooring posts.

cura.1: The doctor put a hand on my forehead. Such cold hands, dear.
cura.2: Healed! And now who'll listen to me, if I don't cough any more?

riserva.1: Good morning, dear! Did you know the ferry was late today?
riserva.2: Ada, dear, are you eating enough? You're thin as tissue paper.
riserva.2d: Miss, dear, are you eating enough? You're thin as tissue paper.
riserva.3: Letters weigh more than people think, dear.
riserva.4: The bell tower is out of tune, but at least it tells the time.

incontro.1: Morning. The bread is in. I've no time.
incontro.2: We've seen each other. That's enough.

consegna.1: A letter. For me. Hasn't happened in years.
consegna.2: Put in the hand. As it should be.

copia.1: Gossip. I knead, I don't listen.
copia.2: The wind carries rumours. The wind doesn't pay for bread.

legge.1: Whoever reads other people's letters has dirty hands. Dirtier than mine.
legge.2: Another envelope opened. I know who did it.

stranezza.2: Me, under her? Not even dead.

nodo.1: Not even the Lord can make me pass that way.
nodo.2: We stood there like two sacks of flour. What a show.

cura.1: The doctor cured Gino. Tomorrow I'll bring him bread.

riserva.1: At six the oven is lit. The rest, we'll see.
riserva.3: Eat, Ada. You don't refuse warm bread.
riserva.3d: Eat, miss. You don't refuse warm bread.
riserva.4: Flour, water, salt. The rest is gossip.

incontro.1: Pax tecum. We meet, and the day is already shorter.
incontro.2: I listened more than I spoke. As always.

consegna.1: Thank you. I'll put it somewhere safe, with the others.
consegna.2: A letter. The Lord knows who it's for. I'll keep it.

copia.1: I heard something. It will stay with me.
copia.2: Rumours come into the church. They don't come out.

legge.1: Reading what is not ours… Deus videt, Teresa.
legge.2: A secret once read never goes back in the envelope.

stranezza.1: I receive everything. I give nothing back. I know, I know.
stranezza.2: The well doesn't speak. But it listens, oh yes.

nodo.1: Two souls stuck on the Fondamenta. Let us pray they move.
nodo.2: A grudge is a knot that tightens when you pull.

cura.1: The doctor does his job. I do mine: I give thanks.
cura.2: Healed. Deo gratias, and thanks to the doctor.

riserva.1: Mass at eleven. The bell rings crooked, but it rings.
riserva.2: Ada, my child, do you sleep at night?
riserva.2d: Miss, do you sleep at night?
riserva.3: I have a drawer full of envelopes. I don't remember putting them there.
riserva.4: Silentium est aureum. My old priest used to say so, and kept quiet.

incontro.1: Hi! Hi! I met everyone, I counted them: seven!
incontro.2: I went right through, zoom! Nobody can catch me!

consegna.1: I carried a letter! I'm a postman!
consegna.2: Delivered! Do I get a sweet?

copia.1: Know what they're saying? I can't tell! But I'll tell.
copia.2: Everyone whispers when I come. But I hear anyway!

legge.1: Teresa reads other people's letters? I want to do it too!
legge.2: A secret! A real secret! I'll keep it. Maybe.

stranezza.2: My feet itch if I stand still!

nodo.1: They got stuck like two posts! So funny!
nodo.2: Mum and Teresa look at each other funny. Why?

cura.1: The doctor gave me bitter medicine. Yuck! But I feel better.
cura.2: No more fever! Can I run? Can I?

riserva.1: I saw a crab this big! I swear!
riserva.2: Ada! Will you teach me to tie knots?
riserva.2d: Miss! Will you teach me to tie knots?
riserva.3: The lighthouse lantern turns all night. Who pushes it?
riserva.4: The bell rang crooked! I'd ring it better!

incontro.2: We've seen each other. The sea's waiting.

consegna.1: A letter. For me? Who writes to a fisherman?

copia.1: Gossip. You don't mend nets with gossip.
copia.2: Somebody talks too much. Not me.

legge.1: Written things belong to whoever wrote them. That's all.
legge.2: Teresa has long eyes. Even the fish know.

stranezza.1: Everyone has their quirks. I have my boat.
stranezza.2: Mh. Strange folk, on this island.

nodo.1: Two who don't speak. Like me and the sea in winter.
nodo.2: If you want to quarrel, do it away from the pier.

cura.1: The foreign doctor. Mh. It works, though.
cura.2: Better. Tomorrow I take the boat out.

riserva.1: The sea's good today. Tomorrow, we'll see.
riserva.2: Nina studies. I fish. That's how it is.
riserva.3: Ada. Here, a fish. For supper.
riserva.3d: Miss. Here, a fish. For supper.
riserva.4: A net always tears where you look least.

incontro.1: Meetings, meetings. This island is a penny serial.
incontro.2: Two words and off. I have a book to finish.

consegna.1: A letter for me! At last something arrives instead of leaving.
consegna.2: Delivered. For once, the world works.

copia.1: Rumours run faster than the ferry. And miss more stops.
copia.2: I know, I know. The whole island knows by now.

legge.1: Reading other people's letters. Not even in nineteenth-century novels.
legge.2: A secret! In books, that's always where the story starts.

stranezza.1: I stay on top and listen. It's called curiosity, not a sin.
stranezza.2: Everyone has a vice. Mine is wanting to know.

nodo.1: Two women who haven't spoken in thirty years. Greek tragedy.
nodo.2: Stuck in the middle of the street. Not even Manzoni would dare.

cura.1: The doctor has a leather bag. In Venice they all have one.
cura.2: Healed. The doctor says I read too much. Oh, really?

riserva.1: Venice is an hour away by ferry. An hour! And it feels like the moon.
riserva.2: Ada, do you read? I'll lend you a book, if you like.
riserva.2d: Miss, do you read? I'll lend you a book, if you like.
riserva.3: Dad says nothing. He says it with silence.
riserva.4: When I grow up I'll be a teacher. For now I'm being patient.

incontro.1: Mh. The light is good this morning.
incontro.2: We meet like boats do: slowly.

consegna.1: A letter… nothing comes to the lighthouse, usually.
consegna.2: Given. The sea brings plenty of letters.

copia.1: Words. The wind brings some and takes some.
copia.2: Gossip doesn't reach the lighthouse. Only the wind.

legge.1: Some people read letters. I read the sea.
legge.2: Some written things are better not known.

stranezza.1: The lighthouse. I don't stray. I can't.
stranezza.2: I have forty years of lighthouse in my legs. They won't go further.

nodo.1: Two who don't speak. Like the tide and the moon.
nodo.2: Water loosens knots. You have to wait.

cura.1: The doctor. Mh. Steady hands, at least.
cura.2: I'm better. The lantern wasn't going to wait.

riserva.1: Last night the sea was smooth. Too smooth.
riserva.2: The lantern turns. I watch. That's all.
riserva.3: Ada… your grandmother called me "the keeper". Only that.
riserva.3d: Miss… your grandmother called me "the keeper". Only that.
riserva.4: Light is seen from far away. That's what it's for.

incontro.1: Good morning! Ettore Lunardi, pharmacist. A real pleasure.
incontro.2: A cordial meeting. I'll make a note of it, as prescribed.

consegna.1: Post for me! From the city, I suppose. How exciting.
consegna.2: Delivered. Perfect, like a dosage properly followed.

copia.1: People murmur, they murmur. In the city it's called "news".
copia.2: Hearsay is as contagious as fever, ladies and gentlemen.

legge.1: Opening other people's post is a crime, you know. Article… I forget which.
legge.2: A secret once read is like an open bottle: it evaporates.

stranezza.1: I never fall ill. A matter of hygiene, and luck.
stranezza.2: I heal from on top. From below, I'm afraid, it doesn't work.

nodo.1: A case of chronic grudge. I prescribe: a coffee together.

cura.1: Two drops, rest and warm broth. Science is simple.
cura.2: Healed! I'll note it in the register. The fourth today.

riserva.1: In the city they called me "doctor". Here, "the pharmacy man".
riserva.2: Miss Ada, isn't it? I have an excellent memory for names.
riserva.2d: The lacemaker, isn't it? Forgive me, the name escapes me.
riserva.3: The lagoon air is good for the lungs. And bad for the mood.
riserva.4: I ordered quinine from the mainland. It'll come on the eight o'clock ferry.

incontro.1: They looked at me the way you look at a stranger. That's fair.
incontro.2: I crossed someone I used to know. He didn't know me.

consegna.1: A letter arrived. Of mine, in fourteen years, not one.
consegna.2: Letters do arrive, sometimes. Someone just has to carry them.

copia.1: Rumours go round like when I was a girl. Nothing changes here.
copia.2: They talk of a woman in black. It's me, and nobody knows.

legge.1: Teresa still reads other people's letters. Some things don't age.
legge.2: On the island, secrets last less than bread.

stranezza.1: My thread goes where it must. I can't stop it any more.
stranezza.2: I'm always on top. Not out of pride: I don't know how to be below.

nodo.1: Two who don't speak. Like my mother and me, for fourteen years.
nodo.2: Knots are tied in a hurry. Untying them is another story.

cura.1: Someone gets better. The day allows that much, at least.
cura.2: A fever gone. You see, my Ada? Not everything is woven.
cura.2d: A fever gone. You see? Not everything is woven.

riserva.1: My Ada, I saw you at the window. I didn't call you.
riserva.1d: There was a girl at the window. I didn't call her.
riserva.2: Chioggia is an hour away by boat. It took me fourteen years.
riserva.3: Sepia black doesn't show on velvet. That was the point.
riserva.4: I learned to weave on my own. Badly, but on my own.
